title_options: Does Deleting Agent Memory Remove Its History? A mem0 Check
mem0 Deletes the Vector, Not the History: What a Read-Back Shows
What mem0's delete() Leaves Behind in the History Table
presentation.title_rationale: A team that promises erasure is really asking whether the delete removed the record of the fact, not only its embedding. The selected title asks that question in the reader's words and names the library and the kind of check, so it is answerable by the page: at the pinned commit the vector entry goes and the history row keeps the deleted text. The body immediately qualifies the scope (static trace, one commit, no runtime probe), so 'A mem0 Check' is not read as a vendor benchmark.
presentation.visual_purpose: A conceptual checklist of the surfaces this article audits, in the order the argument visits them: vector entry, history records, read-back checks. It explains why a success return is not evidence of erasure; it shows no measurements, no counts and no claim to cover every place a copy can survive.
